correctness.rationale: For 0<rho<1, a=(1+rho)/2, d=(1-rho)/2, eta>=1 and fixed alpha>0, independent signed binomial imbalance T has ET=0 and ET^2=1/eta. Squaring the exact coordinate update yields B=[[ (1-alpha*a)^2, alpha^2*a*d/eta ],[alpha^2*a*d/eta,(1-alpha*d)^2]]. Its strictly positive off-diagonals make the Perron eigenvalue the asymptotic kth-root mean square for every nonzero deterministic error, rather than merely a worst-case bound. Direct diagonalization gives the stated radical r_eta. det(I-B)=alpha^2*a*d[4-2alpha+alpha^2*a*d(1-eta^-2)] and strict spectral convexity give the exact stable interval alpha<4/(1+sqrt(rho^2+(1-rho^2)/eta^2)), with equality nondecay and larger alpha divergence. The conditional norm matrix E(I-alpha G)^2 gives a smaller alpha_step=4/(1+rho+(1-rho)/eta), strictly smaller when eta>1. Derivatives at alpha=1 and 2 plus strict convexity give unique alpha_opt in (1,2). An independent batch-count calculation matched the exact moment recursion and radical eigenvalue on 192 finite comparisons; this verifies representative cases, not the universal domain.
